name: handler_cli
title: Progression Handler: Progress Reported via 'cli' Progress Bars (Text) in the Terminal

arguments.name: show_after
arguments.text: Seconds to wait before displaying the bar. The body never reads this formal; the reporter uses enable_after.

arguments.name: intrusiveness
arguments.text: How disruptive the reporter is. The default is the option progressr.intrusiveness.terminal, or 1.

arguments.name: target
arguments.text: Where progress is rendered. The default is "terminal".

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Chooses the format and format_done strings unless format is passed explicitly. match.arg accepts a unique prefix.
Named arguments for cli_progress_bar and make_progression_handler. A total of 0 does not call cli.

origin.details: type default leaves the cli format unset. steps, percent, and time each set a format and a format_done string. The bar is erased when clear is TRUE and a newline is written when clear is FALSE.
origin.example:
h <- handler_cli(type = "steps", enable = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("handler_cli steps is %s.\n", class(h)[1]))

translation.description: Report progress with the translated cli_progress_bar.

arguments.name: show_after
arguments.text: Accepted and stored. The reporter waits on enable_after, which is what the R body reads.

arguments.name: intrusiveness
arguments.text: How disruptive the reporter is. The default is the option progressr.intrusiveness.terminal, or 1.

arguments.name: target
arguments.text: Where progress is rendered. The default is "terminal".

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Chooses the format and format_done strings unless format is passed explicitly. A unique prefix matches.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: Named arguments for cli_progress_bar and make_progression_handler. A total of 0 does not call cli.

translation.details: type default leaves the format unset. steps, percent, and time each set a format and a format_done string. In a non-dynamic session the translated cli bar returns an id and does not draw, so the stderr is the newline or the erase this handler writes itself.
translation.value: A calling handler whose first class is cli_progression_handler.
translation.example:
from progressr.cli_handlers import handler_cli

handler = handler_cli(type="steps", enable=True)
print(f"handler_cli steps is {handler.classes[0]}.")
